newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rand Mines sinks on suspension news.
newsitem.headline: Rand Mines sinks on suspension news.

text.p: Rand Mines Ltd sank more than 16 percent on Wednesday morning to a new year low after announcing it would suspend its listing ahead of a proposed winding-up of the company.

Rand Mines was down five cents to 26 cents, inching off its new year low of 24 cents with more than a million shares changing hands on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. The share was the second biggest loser by percentage.
Dealers said Rand Mines has been coming off steadily since January when it touched a year high of 90 cents.
"Yes, it's quite a bit down but this news has been in the market for quite a while now and it has been losing value since the start of the year," one dealer said.
Rand Mines announced earlier that its listing in the cash sector of the JSE would be suspended on May 22 ahead of the proposed winding-up of the company.
The group said its listing on the London Stock Exchange would also be suspended on that day.
"It's falling basically because the guys are baling out ahead of the winding down," a dealer said.
The announcement comes after news at the end of April that a possible offer for the company had been withdrawn.
Rand Mines suffered its biggest slide in the immediate aftermath of the offer's withdrawal on April 24 when it plunged more than 35 percent to 40 cents.
